CVE-2026-109618.summary: Unauthenticated remote code execution via out-of-memory corruption during request initialization and cleanup.

CVE-2026-109619.summary: Unauthenticated remote code execution via stale global state across reused worker processes.

sapi_risk_ranking.mod_php: highest (attack can run during request startup before application code with default memory and input limits)
sapi_risk_ranking.frankenphp: high (similar to mod_php by source analysis)
sapi_risk_ranking.cgi: affected (any PHP SAPI serving web requests)
sapi_risk_ranking.cli: low (not directly serving web requests unless wrapped by an HTTP worker)

affected.notes: No configuration mitigation fully blocks attacks. Patching and restarting all workers is the only complete defense.

branches.notes: No official release. PHP published minimal source backports for 8.1 that vendors must package and validate.
No official release. PHP published minimal source backports for 8.0 that vendors must package and validate.
No official release. PHP published minimal source backports for 7.4 that vendors must package and validate.
End-of-life branch with no official release or upstream source backport. Earliest affected path dates to PHP 5.4.0.

mitigations.title: Upgrade to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 and restart all workers
mitigations.notes: The only complete fix. Rebuild containers and restart or replace every PHP worker so old code does not stay in memory.

mitigations.title: Enforce memory_limit=-1 administratively via php_admin_value
mitigations.notes: Removes controllable PHP memory_limit failure. Pair with frontend request size limits and container/cgroup memory boundaries. Other allocation failures can still reach the bug.

mitigations.title: Use container or cgroup memory limits, never RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA
mitigations.notes: Use cgroup MemoryMax or container mem_limit as the availability boundary. Avoid ulimit -v, LimitAS, and LimitDATA which trigger in-process allocation failures.

mitigations.title: Enforce frontend request size limits and post_max_size
mitigations.notes: Enforce strict request and decoded body size limits at the reverse proxy and PHP post_max_size (for example 8M, tuned to upload requirements).

mitigations.title: Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 before request parsing
mitigations.notes: Covers one confirmed path of CVE-2026-109619. Must be set in configuration loaded before request parsing, followed by worker restart. Reduces exposure; does not replace patching.

mitigations.title: Set fatal_error_backtraces=0 on PHP 8.5
mitigations.notes: PHP 8.5 only. Set in startup configuration loaded before request parsing and restart workers.

mitigations.title: Remove per-request INI overrides that produce early diagnostics
mitigations.notes: Remove .htaccess php_value/php_flag under mod_php and FastCGI PHP_VALUE/PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameters in Nginx that can trigger early startup warnings.

mitigations.title: Apply reverse proxy or WAF rules blocking anomalous multipart/form-urlencoded payloads
mitigations.notes: Blocks known exploit shapes (oversized form field names, control bytes in form fields, ~3.5 MB form fields). Can be bypassed; reduces exposure only.

mitigations.title: Enable aggressive worker recycling (pm.max_requests and scheduled FPM reloads)
mitigations.notes: Lowers the probability that consecutive requests reach the same stale worker state for CVE-2026-109619. Does nothing for CVE-2026-109618.

mitigations.title: Isolate or restrict public network access to unpatched PHP applications
mitigations.notes: Place internal or legacy PHP applications behind VPN, Zero Trust access, or IP allowlists while migration is prepared.

mitigations.title: Evaluate verified vendor-patched builds for EOL PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1
mitigations.notes: PHP published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1. HeroDevs NES lists a patch for CVE-2026-109618. Verify any vendor or distro build against both CVE IDs.
